english.title: Wear/display item of clothing/article on relevant premises supporting proscribed organisation
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), on relevant premises, namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..),

(A)_[wore an item of clothing,]_
(B)_[wore, carried or displayed an article,]_
(C)_[wore an item of clothing and wore, carried or displayed an article,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY DETAILS..), in such a way or in such circumstances as to arouse reasonable suspicion that you were a member or supporter of a proscribed organisation, namely **(..SPECIFY ORGANISATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 13(1)(ZA) and (3) of the Terrorism Act 2000.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Attorney General is required, section 117 of the Terrorism Act 2000.
(ii) See section 13(8) of the Act for a list of relevant premises and Schedule 2 for a list of proscribed organisations.
(iii) For UK-wide jurisdiction for this offence regardless of where it took place see section 28 of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008.
(iv) See also the offences regarding public places of wearing item of clothing in section 13(1)(a) (H3556) and of wearing/carrying article in section 13(1)(b) (H3557).

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

Since 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.
